cover: Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: wide editorial cover for a technical article, aspect ratio 2.4:1. Create an original illustration matching a classic engineering notebook: warm ivory paper, precise dark navy pen-and-ink hatching, restrained cobalt blue, vermilion and ochre, generous margins. Left half: large legible classic serif headline, exact text "When a higher eval score means worse work". Smaller serif subtitle "Reward hacking in agent evaluations". Right half: a nineteenth-century precision balance on an engineer’s desk. One pan holds a carefully drawn small machine part; the other holds a stack of inspection tickets with cobalt checkmarks. A detached calibration weight sits conspicuously beside the balance, marked with a small vermilion cross, suggesting the measurement has been altered. Brass instruments, a folded technical drawing and a notebook, sparse composition. This is a metaphor for a corrupted measurement, not a numerical chart. Clear hierarchy, crisp readable type, no modern UI cards, robots, gradients, watermark, signature, charts, extra labels or dash punctuation. Keep the entire headline inside safe margins.
two_routes: Use case: scientific-educational. Asset type: original explanatory diagram for a technical article, landscape approximately 1.8:1. Style: warm ivory paper, precise dark navy pen-and-ink engineering hatching, large classic serif typography, restrained cobalt blue checkmarks, vermilion crosses and ochre rules. Match the style of an illustrated engineering notebook, no UI cards. Title exact: "Two routes to passing tests". Two spacious columns separated by a thin ochre vertical rule. Left heading "Fix the code". Show a sheet labeled "pricing.py" with a small navy correction mark and a cobalt check beside it. Beneath it an untouched inspection ledger labeled "Original tests". Bottom of this column exact text "Tests pass" with cobalt check and then "Discount works" with cobalt check. Right heading "Change the checks". Show an untouched sheet labeled "pricing.py", beside it an inspection ledger labeled "Edited tests" with a crossed-out expected value and an obvious vermilion pencil. Bottom of this column exact text "Tests pass" with cobalt check and then "Discount still broken" with vermilion cross. Simple straight downward arrows in each column, no crossing connections. Bottom centered caption exact: "A green result does not tell us what changed". The diagram is a constructed example, not a report of measured model behavior. Make labels legible on mobile, use few visual elements, all text spelled exactly, no extra numerical examples, robots, logos, gradients, watermark, signature or punctuation dashes.
independent_evaluation: Use case: scientific-educational. Asset type: high-level architecture diagram for an article about trustworthy coding-agent evaluations. Landscape approximately 1.8:1. Original classic technical illustration on warm ivory paper, dark navy pen-and-ink hatching, cobalt and ochre accents, large legible serif lettering. Title exact "Keep the measurement outside the work". Left half: open drafting workbench bounded by a thin navy outline, heading "Agent workspace", two paper sheets labeled "pricing.py" and "Local checks". Right half: a separate enclosed inspection bench bounded by a navy outline with a small brass lock icon, heading "Independent evaluation", sheets labeled "Original requirements" and "Additional checks", small register labeled "Allowed edits". Between the halves: exactly one straight rightward cobalt arrow labeled "Copy the implementation". Inside right half, the copy of pricing.py flows down through the checks to a final ledger labeled "Result and reasons". Bottom caption exact "Check the behavior and the permitted changes". Clear separation of work and evaluation, simple straight arrows, only specified text, generous whitespace, no overlapping connections, no charts, robots, extra text, dashboard UI cards, gradients, watermark or signature. The lock is conceptual; do not claim this drawing is a real security boundary or a sandbox.
